proposals.before: Shi Hu was greatly pleased, appointed him General Who Uplifts the Army, and entrusted him with affairs in the west.
proposals.after: Shi Hu was greatly pleased, appointed him Champion General, and entrusted him with affairs in the west.
proposals.reason: 冠軍將軍 is the Champion General title; Uplifts the Army mistranslates 冠軍.

proposals.before: Some urged Hong to assume the supreme title; Hong also because a prophecy read “grass-payment shall answer as king,” and moreover his grandson Jian bore on his back the characters “grass-payment,” changed his surname to Fu, and styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of the Three Qins.
proposals.after: Some urged Hong to assume the supreme title; Hong also because a prophecy read “grass-Fu shall answer as king,” and moreover his grandson Jian bore on his back the characters “grass-Fu,” changed his surname to Fu, and styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of the Three Qins.
proposals.reason: 草付 is the graphic analysis of 苻 (grass radical plus 付), not payment; the idiomatic line already has grass-Fu.

proposals.before: Jian meant to take Guanzhong but hid it from Du Hong: he took a sham post from Shi Zhi, built at Fangtou, and forced everyone to plant wheat as proof he would not march west—slackers were executed pour encourager les autres.
proposals.after: Jian meant to take Guanzhong but hid it from Du Hong: he took a sham post from Shi Zhi, built at Fangtou, and forced everyone to plant wheat as proof he would not march west—slackers were executed as a warning.
proposals.reason: The French tag invents a literary flourish absent from the Chinese, which only says he killed non-planters as a warning (以徇).

proposals.before: Lady Qiang became queen; Crown Prince Chang succeeded in line; Xiong became chancellor, supreme commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Yong; the rest took posts by rank.
proposals.after: He established his wife Lady Qiang as queen of the Heavenly King, his son Chang as the Heavenly King’s crown prince, and his brother Xiong as chancellor, commander of all armies, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and concurrent Governor of Yong; the rest received graded appointments.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic ‘Crown Prince Chang succeeded in line’ invents a succession; the Chinese only records that Jian established his son Chang as 天王皇太子.

proposals.before: Revolt flared: Kong Te at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xia Houqi at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyandu at Bashicheng—each mustered tens of thousands—and all begged Huan Wen and Yin Hao for relief.
proposals.after: Revolt flared: Kong Te at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each mustered tens of thousands—and all begged Huan Wen and Yin Hao for relief.
proposals.reason: 夏侯顯 is the surname-compound Xiahou plus given name Xian, not ‘Xia Houqi’; 呼延毒 is the surname Huyan plus given name Du, not the fused Huyandu.

proposals.before: Thereupon Kong Te rose at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xia Houqi at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyandu at Bashicheng—each with tens of thousands—and all sent envoys to General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen and Central Army commander Yin Hao begging rescue.
proposals.after: Thereupon Kong Te rose at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each with tens of thousands—and all sent envoys to General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen and Central Army commander Yin Hao begging rescue.
proposals.reason: Same name errors as the idiomatic line: 夏侯顯 and 呼延毒 are mis-segmented in English.

proposals.before: He detached Xiong with seven thousand cavalry to meet Huan Chong on Bailuyuan and shattered the Jin horse; Sima Xun was beaten again in Zigug.
proposals.after: He detached Xiong with seven thousand cavalry to meet Huan Chong on Bailuyuan and shattered the imperial army; Sima Xun was beaten again in Ziwu Valley.
proposals.reason: 王師敗績 is the Jin imperial army routed, not 'Jin horse'; 子午穀 is Ziwu Valley, not Zigug.

proposals.before: Jian separately had Xiong lead seven thousand horse to fight Huan Chong at Bailuyuan; the imperial army was routed; he also broke Sima Xun in Zigug valley.
proposals.after: Jian separately had Xiong lead seven thousand horse to fight Huan Chong at Bailuyuan; the imperial army was routed; he also broke Sima Xun in Ziwu valley.
proposals.reason: 子午穀 is Ziwu valley; Zigug is a corrupted transcription.

proposals.before: The same year the western leader Qimojunxie sent a son as hostage, and Jian opened a state guesthouse at Pingpuo Gate to impress distant peoples.
proposals.after: The same year the western leader Qimojunxie sent a son as hostage, and Jian opened a state guesthouse at Pingshuo Gate to impress distant peoples.
proposals.reason: 平朔門 is Pingshuo Gate; Pingpuo misreads 朔.

proposals.before: That year the western tribesman Qimojunxie sent his son as hostage; Jian built the Guest Reception Lodge at Pingpuo Gate to court those from afar.
proposals.after: That year the western tribesman Qimojunxie sent his son as hostage; Jian built the Guest Reception Lodge at Pingshuo Gate to court those from afar.
proposals.reason: 平朔門 is Pingshuo Gate, not Pingpuo.

proposals.before: Horses and oxes chewed one another’s coats; wolves and brutes preyed on men; highways went dead.
proposals.after: Horses and oxen chewed one another’s coats; wolves and brutes preyed on men; highways went dead.
proposals.reason: 'Oxes' is ungrammatical for 牛馬.

proposals.before: He then named Chang’s son Sheng heir apparent.
proposals.after: He then named his son Sheng heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 其子生 is Jian's son Sheng (健第三子 in s0103–s0105), not Chang's son.

proposals.before: Thereupon he established Chang’s son Sheng as crown prince.
proposals.after: Thereupon he established his son Sheng as crown prince.
proposals.reason: Following 太子萇's death, 立其子生 means Jian established his own son Sheng; later units state Sheng was Jian's third son.

proposals.before: Lü Lou became palace attendant and left grand general; Fu An took the grand commandant’s seal; Fu Liu held Bing as eastern conqueror from Puban; Fu Sou held Yu from Shancheng; others were ranked accordingly.
proposals.after: Lü Polou became palace attendant and left grand general; Fu An took the grand commandant’s seal; Fu Liu held Bing as eastern conqueror from Puban; Fu Sou held Yu from Shancheng; others were ranked accordingly.
proposals.reason: 呂婆樓 is Lü Polou; dropping 婆 yields the wrong personal name.

proposals.before: The Jin prince wishes together with the Zhang kings to share the bright sun, exchange silks as friendship, and with you, lord, swear a bond like metal and orchid—therefore he has come from afar; what is strange in that!”
proposals.after: The Jin prince wishes together with the Zhang kings to share the bright sun, exchange silks as friendship, and with you, lord, swear a bond like metal and orchid—therefore we have come from afar; what is strange in that!”
proposals.reason: Chinese 不遠而來 is the envoys’ coming, not the Prince of Jin in person; the idiomatic version already has ‘we have come’.

proposals.before: those who combine civil and martial talent, vessels of the divine regalia, outstanding in person—within they can harmonize the hundred crafts, without they can shatter enemy hosts at ten thousand li—are the younger brothers of the General of the Guards, Prince of Guangping, Fu Huangmei, the General of the Rear, Prince of Qinghe, Fu Fa, and the General of the Soaring Dragon, Prince of Donghai, Fu Jian;
proposals.after: those who combine civil and martial talent, vessels of the divine regalia, outstanding in person—within they can harmonize the hundred crafts, without they can shatter enemy hosts at ten thousand li—are the brothers the General of the Guards, Prince of Guangping, Fu Huangmei; the General of the Rear, Prince of Qinghe, Fu Fa; and the General of the Soaring Dragon, Prince of Donghai, Fu Jian;
proposals.reason: 之兄弟 names Huangmei, Fa, and Jian as the brothers themselves, matching the idiomatic rendering; the literal wrongly makes them uncles of unnamed younger brothers.

proposals.before: those clear in talent and judgment, whose orders are obeyed and prohibitions enforced, are Special Companion and concurrent Censor-in-chief Liang Pinglao, Special Companion and Grand Master of Splendid Carriages Qiang Wang, and Palace Attendant and Minister Lü Lou;
proposals.after: those clear in talent and judgment, whose orders are obeyed and prohibitions enforced, are Special Companion and concurrent Censor-in-chief Liang Pinglao, Special Companion and Grand Master of Splendid Carriages Qiang Wang, and Palace Attendant and Minister Lü Polou;
proposals.reason: 呂婆樓 is the three-character personal name Lü Polou; ‘Lü Lou’ drops 婆.

proposals.before: those rich in pattern and history, luxuriant as literary patriarchs, are Right Vice Director Dong Rong, Palace Library Director Wang Yang, and Editorial Director Liang Dan;
proposals.after: those rich in pattern and history, luxuriant as literary patriarchs, are Right Vice Director Dong Rong, Palace Library Director Wang Yang, and Editorial Director Liang Dang;
proposals.reason: 梁讜 is Dang, as in the idiomatic line; Dan is a wrong transcription.

proposals.before: To slight the great and serve the small is what the Spring and Autumn condemns—only you, lord, should plan it.”
proposals.after: That the small should fail to serve the great is what the Spring and Autumn condemns—only you, lord, should plan it.”
proposals.reason: 小不事大 means the small not serving the great; the literal reverses the hierarchy.

proposals.before: With rebellion along the frontier and Qin looming, Zhang Guan persuaded Zhang Xuanjing to submit; Fu Sheng accepted the vassal’s titles.
proposals.after: Zhang Guan, newly taking up the auxiliary government, feared Qin’s army as troops rose throughout Hexi, so he advised Zhang Xuanjing to send envoys declaring vassalage; Fu Sheng invested them according to the titles they claimed.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 新輔政 and 河西, and omits that Sheng conferred office according to the titles Liang itself declared.

proposals.before: Guan had newly taken up auxiliary government; troops rose everywhere along the River-west; he feared Qin’s army would arrive; therefore he spoke to Xuanjing, sent envoys to declare vassalage, and Sheng according to their declaration invested them.”
proposals.after: Guan had newly taken up auxiliary government; troops rose everywhere along the River-west; he feared Qin’s army would arrive; therefore he spoke to Xuanjing, sent envoys to declare vassalage, and Sheng according to their declaration invested them.
proposals.reason: The literal English ends with a stray unmatched closing quotation mark not present as a quotation frame in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Sheng thought he mocked Our eye, bored out Yan’s eyes, then beheaded him.
proposals.after: Sheng thought he mocked his eye, bored out Yan’s eyes, then beheaded him.
proposals.reason: 其目 is Sheng’s own eye in third-person narration; Our eye invents an imperial first-person the Chinese does not use here.

proposals.before: Huangmei grew angry, plotted to kill Sheng and set himself up; the affair leaked; he was executed by strangulation; many of the princes, dukes, and kin died.
proposals.after: Huangmei grew angry, plotted to kill Sheng and set himself up; the affair leaked; he was executed; many of the princes, dukes, and kin died.
proposals.reason: 伏誅 means he was put to death; the Chinese does not specify strangulation.

proposals.before: Courtiers who praised his sage rule—
proposals.after: Those at his side who said Your Majesty sagely illumines the age and the realm alone sings of great peace—
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line is truncated and drops the quoted address 陛下聖明宰世，天下惟歌太平 that the Chinese and literal still carry.

proposals.before: The maid warned Fu Fa; with Liang Pinglao and Qiang Wang he seized the Cloud Dragon Gate as Fu Jian and Lü Lou stormed in—guards threw down their weapons for Fu Jian.
proposals.after: The maid warned Fu Fa; with Liang Pinglao and Qiang Wang he seized the Cloud Dragon Gate as Fu Jian and Lü Polou stormed in—guards threw down their weapons for Fu Jian.
proposals.reason: 呂婆樓 is Lü Polou; shortening the given name to Lou invents a different English personal name.

proposals.before: When the attending maid came to report, he then with Special Companion Liang Pinglao, Qiang Wang, and others led several hundred stalwarts to slip into the Cloud Dragon Gate; Fu Jian and Lü Lou led more than three hundred of their command shouting and pressing forward; the night-watch generals and soldiers all cast aside staves and submitted to Jian.
proposals.after: When the attending maid came to report, he then with Special Companion Liang Pinglao, Qiang Wang, and others led several hundred stalwarts to slip into the Cloud Dragon Gate; Fu Jian and Lü Polou led more than three hundred of their command shouting and pressing forward; the night-watch generals and soldiers all cast aside staves and submitted to Jian.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise renders 呂婆樓 as Lü Lou instead of Lü Polou.

proposals.before: When Jian’s host had arrived, they led Sheng forth and placed him in a separate chamber, deposed him as Prince of Yue, and before long killed him.
proposals.after: When Jian’s host had arrived, they led Sheng forth and placed him in a separate chamber, deposed him and made him Prince of Yue, and before long killed him.
proposals.reason: 廢之為越王 is demotion to Prince of Yue, not removal from that title; the current literal reverses the office change.

proposals.before: He loathed Dong Rong and his fellow favorite Zhao Shao—ministers who had wormed into power—and cut them dead at every audience.
proposals.after: He loathed Dong Rong and Qiang Guo as mortal foes, and at every court audience he would not speak to them at all.
proposals.reason: Chinese 強國 is Qiang Guo; Zhao Shao and the invented ‘wormed into power’ clause are not in the source (the literal already has Qiang Guo).

decisions.reason: 冠軍將軍 is the Champion General office; “Uplifts the Army” invents a wrong gloss of 冠軍.

decisions.reason: 立子萇為天王皇太子 records an appointment, not that Chang “succeeded in line.” The replacement restores wife, son, brother, and 領雍州刺史.

decisions.reason: 夏侯顯 is Xiahou Xian and 呼延毒 is Huyan Du; Xia Houqi and Huyandu mis-segment the names.

The literal likewise misreads 平朔門 as Pingpuo.
“Oxes” is ungrammatical English for 牛馬; oxen is the needed correction.
至是，立其子生為太子 has 其子 referring to Jian after 太子萇 died, not Chang’s son.
The same 其子生 error appears in the literal field.
呂婆樓 is the three-character name Lü Polou; dropping 婆 yields a false personal name.

decisions.after: those who combine civil and martial talent, vessels of the divine regalia, outstanding in person—within they can harmonize the hundred crafts, without they can shatter enemy hosts at ten thousand li—are the brothers General of the Guards, Prince of Guangping, Fu Huangmei; General of the Rear, Prince of Qinghe, Fu Fa; and General of the Soaring Dragon, Prince of Donghai, Fu Jian;
decisions.reason: 之兄弟 identifies Huangmei, Fa, and Jian themselves as the brothers; the original makes them uncles. The proposal’s “the brothers the General” is still awkward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 衛大將軍、廣平王黃眉，後將軍、清河王法，龍驤將軍、東海王堅之兄弟

decisions.reason: 侍中、尚書呂婆樓 is Lü Polou, not Lü Lou.
梁讜 is Dang; Dan is a wrong transcription of 讜.
小不事大 is the small failing to serve the great; the original reverses the Spring and Autumn maxim.
The original omits 新輔政, 河西所在兵起, and 生因其所稱而授之; the replacement restores those facts.

decisions.reason: This unit is narrative, not a closing quotation; the stray English quote mark is not in the Chinese.
譏其目 is third-person “his eye”; “Our eye” invents imperial first person.

The idiomatic line is truncated and drops 陛下聖明宰世，天下惟歌太平.

claimRetractions.reason: The English personal name Lü Lou was produced only by dropping 婆 from 呂婆樓; the source supports Lü Polou, already recorded as c0450.
Liang Dan is a mistranscription of 梁讜; the source supports Liang Dang (c0461), not a separate given name Dan.
Lü Lou is the same dropped-婆 error for 呂婆樓; no source-based alias remains besides Lü Polou.
Zhao Shao exists only in the bad idiomatic English; the Chinese names 強國 (Qiang Guo).

claimRevisions.reason: Repair restores the surname-compound Xiahou Xian for 夏侯顯; Xia Houqi was a translation segmentation error.
Xiahou Xian is now explicit in the repaired English, not merely inferred.
呼延毒 is surname Huyan plus given name Du, not the fused Huyandu.
Huyan Du is now explicit in the repaired English.
The extracted English name Lü Lou dropped 婆 from 呂婆樓; the repaired line restores Lü Polou.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以呂婆樓為侍中、左大將軍

claimRevisions.reason: With Lü Lou retracted, Lü Polou is the explicit English rendering of 呂婆樓 in the repaired units.
